topic.name: The 2x2 Inverse Formula
later_kps: kp3: Singularity via the determinant condition

kp_block.name: Applying the formula
kp_block.constraints: prefer ad - bc = +-1 for integer inverses

teach_page.concept: For a 2 by 2 matrix the inverse has a closed formula. The determinant $ad - bc$ measures the area scale of the matrix, and the inverse must undo that scale, so each entry of the swapped matrix is divided by the determinant.

worked_example.problem: Find $A^{-1}$ for $A = \begin{pmatrix}3&2\\7&5\end{pmatrix}$. Give the matrix as [a,b;c,d].
steps: Swap the diagonal entries: $3$ and $5$ change places.
Change the sign of the other two entries: $2$ becomes $-2$ and $7$ becomes $-7$.
Divide by the determinant: each entry divided by $1$ gives [5,-2;-7,3].

existing.solution_sketch: $ad - bc = 6 - 5 = 1$; swap the diagonal, negate the off-diagonal, divide by $1$. Check: $AA^{-1} = I$.

diagnostic_problem: Find $A^{-1}$ for $A = \begin{pmatrix}4&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$, and state the value of $k$ for which $\begin{pmatrix}4&2\\3&k\end{pmatrix}$ would have no inverse.
